journey.solution: Next.js on Vercel, plus Domains API, ISR, Edge Middleware, and Preview Deployments, removed the scaling and deployment blockers.

outcome: Improved performance and reliability with a more flexible ecommerce stack

journey.before: Tekla had buggy, slow builds on Gatsby Cloud and used WooCommerce for ecommerce.
journey.goal: Handle growing traffic while delivering personalized experiences and owning more of the ecommerce journey.
journey.change: The existing setup needed more reliable performance and flexibility for Tekla’s ecommerce needs.
journey.solution: Tekla moved its site to Vercel and its commerce backend to Medusa; Next.js is planned for Tekla, while Agilo uses it on other projects.

outcome: Builds cut from a full day to two minutes

journey.before: Tray.ai’s legacy site used an outdated Next.js version, Serverless, siloed repos, and a rigid pipeline that made builds slow and unreliable.
journey.goal: Modernize the marketing site, unify content and form management, and support more than 500,000 pages.
journey.change: Full-deploy previews, separate form logic, frequent build failures, and day-long build times blocked fast iteration.
journey.solution: Roboto Studio rebuilt the site with Next.js and Turborepo on Vercel, using Preview Deployments, Vercel Functions, Web Analytics, Speed Insights, and Firewall.

outcome: 5× faster builds; uncached page loads fell from 60 seconds to ~3 seconds

journey.before: Leonardo.AI faced 10+ minute builds, slow uncached pages, and frequent outages, while both startups operated without dedicated DevOps teams.
journey.goal: They aimed to serve users globally and keep shipping without hiring infrastructure teams.
journey.change: Infrastructure work and manual provisioning were diverting engineering time, while DevOps talent was costly and difficult to find.
journey.solution: Vercel handled provisioning and scaling; Leonardo.AI used Observability with Fluid compute, and Relevance AI demonstrated building and deploying an agent with v0.

outcome: Built an AI-powered brand assistant with real-time streaming and interactive content

journey.before: Sitecore was evaluating AI SDKs while building a brand assistant with a Python backend and a Next.js frontend.
journey.goal: Sitecore wanted marketers to interact conversationally with brand assets and create on-brand content.
journey.change: The team needed to connect backend AI capabilities with an engaging frontend that streamed responses in real time.
journey.solution: The AI SDK and Next.js brought streaming chat UI and interactive AI experiences together with Sitecore's Azure-hosted backend.

outcome: Supports both SSE and Streamable HTTP for Vapi’s MCP server

journey.before: Vapi’s MCP server was deployed to support only Server-Sent Events transport.
journey.goal: Vapi wanted to make integrating its voice-agent capabilities into workflows frictionless.
journey.change: The server needed to support the newer Streamable HTTP transport as well as SSE, without adding infrastructure overhead.
journey.solution: Vapi rebuilt the server with Vercel’s MCP Adapter and deployed it on Vercel, using Fluid compute to reuse resources across client connections.

outcome: 60% increase in site traffic after a zero-downtime migration

journey.before: A sole developer maintained 30 web properties on an unreliable Ruby on Rails monolith deployed to a physical server.
journey.goal: Improve SEO and reduce infrastructure management so the lean team could focus on user and brand experiences.
journey.change: Outages during maintenance or traffic spikes and manual SSL certificate reviews across 30 domains consumed time and threatened reliability.
journey.solution: They migrated to Next.js on Vercel’s managed infrastructure and used ISR to manage tens of thousands of articles.

outcome: 10x faster development and 25x lower costs vs. PHP/WordPress monoliths

journey.before: Each client had a separate server, CMS, and custom website, creating duplicated work and infrastructure.
journey.goal: Manage a multilingual, multi-brand portfolio and onboard new clients quickly using a shared workflow.
journey.change: Client-by-client infrastructure and bespoke sites made it difficult to reuse code and data efficiently.
journey.solution: Wunderman Thompson combines Next.js components in a Turborepo monorepo with DatoCMS and Vercel’s serverless platform.
